journal: IOP Conference Series: Materials Science and Engineering
title: Activated carbons from oil palm shell for hydrogen storage
material_description: Oil palm shell | AC4 (also called 'lab made AC'/'lab-made AC'): activated carbon from oil palm shell charcoal (OPC; oil palm shell carbonized at 650 °C for 1 h under N2) chemically activated with KOH at weight ratio KOH/OPC W = 4, 800 °C for 2 h; the only AC of the series measured for H2
purification_method: precursor washed with water and sun-dried; activated product washed with distilled water, then HCl (1 M), then distilled water until the rinse pH stabilised, oven-dried 12 h, stored in a vacuum desiccator
activation_method: KOH chemical activation: OPC ground and sieved to 100-200 µm, mixed with KOH at weight ratio KOH/OPC = 4, heated in a nickel crucible in a muffle furnace at 3 °C/min to 800 °C and held 2 h under N2 (300 mL/min)
source_location: main-6.png (printed p. 5), Figure 3a, black squares (AC4, 77 K, up to 1 bar), marker 1 of 22 (origin)
notes: archive: HYC-0084_fig3a_AC4_77K_low_pressure.json; origin marker digitized at 0.00032080659945001456 bar, -0.0071856287425145614 wt% (negative value within digitization error of zero, stored as 0 because uptake_wt_pct must be >= 0); a marker at zero pressure is likely a plotted origin rather than a measurement, so value_kind unclear; I1 = Figure 3a low-pressure isotherm (up to 1 bar) measured on the Micromeritics ASAP 2020 HD88 (Section 2.3.2); basis_inferred excess by the volumetric instrumental default; 22 markers counted and 22 extracted; the single Figure 3 series is assigned to AC4 because Section 3.2 states that only AC4 was considered for hydrogen storage analysis (the same paragraph mentions isotherms 'of the BC and ACs', but each panel shows one series); Characterization from Table 1 (main-4.png, p. 3), N2 at 77 K on Micromeritics ASAP 2020: S_BET 3503 m2/g (abstract prints 3508 m2/g; Table 1, Section 3.1 text, Section 3.3 and Table 2 print 3503); micropore volume = V_DR (DR) 1.10 cm3/g; total pore volume = V0.99 1.68 cm3/g; Vmeso 0.58 cm3/g (= V0.99 - V_DR); EA (characteristic energy) 20.24 kJ/mol; average micropore diameter L0 1.22 nm (printed L0 values match Stoeckli L0 = 10.8/(E0 - 11.4) applied to the printed EA); V_DR/V0.99 0.66; S_BET and pore volumes with a 'typical, maximum, uncertainty of 3 %'; BET applied to the adsorption branch, no P/P0 range printed; N2 outgassing 523 K for 48 h; H2 degassing: 'outgassed under a primary vacuum at 350 °C for 24 h' (no end pressure printed); uncertainty: 'Repeatability was always found to be very satisfactory, leading to errors lower than 3% on each measurement' (relative, so uncertainty_wt_pct left empty); basis not named in the paper; pressure not called gauge, taken as absolute; measuring_lab_id from the corresponding-author mark (*) on M Fan, although the printed corresponding e-mail is weigang-zhao@fafu.edu.cn

material_description: Oil palm shell | AC4 (also called 'lab made AC'/'lab-made AC'): activated carbon from oil palm shell charcoal (OPC; oil palm shell carbonized at 650 °C for 1 h under N2) chemically activated with KOH at weight ratio KOH/OPC W = 4, 800 °C for 2 h; the only AC of the series measured for H2
purification_method: precursor washed with water and sun-dried; activated product washed with distilled water, then HCl (1 M), then distilled water until the rinse pH stabilised, oven-dried 12 h, stored in a vacuum desiccator
activation_method: KOH chemical activation: OPC ground and sieved to 100-200 µm, mixed with KOH at weight ratio KOH/OPC = 4, heated in a nickel crucible in a muffle furnace at 3 °C/min to 800 °C and held 2 h under N2 (300 mL/min)
source_location: main-6.png (printed p. 5), Figure 3b, black squares (AC4, 77 K, up to 8 MPa), blob 9 of 12 (blob 1 is the origin marker, not stored)
notes: archive: HYC-0084_fig3b_AC4_77K_high_pressure.json; digitized x = 4.159357982229866 MPa; I2 = Figure 3b high-pressure isotherm (up to 8 MPa) measured on the HPVA-100 (VTI Corporation of TA Instruments), which the paper calls 'the gravimetric analyzer HPVA-100'; coded gravimetric_microbalance as printed (the instrument name suggests a volumetric analyzer; flag for reconciliation); no buoyancy correction or free-volume calibration stated, so basis_inferred unknown; 15 markers counted, 12 blobs digitized, 11 rows (the origin marker digitized at a pressure <= 0 and is not stored; three pairs of overlapping markers near 0.68, 1.35 and 2.69 MPa could not be separated; see log.md); digitized pressure in MPa converted to bar (x 10); the single series is assigned to AC4 because Section 3.2 states that only AC4 was considered for hydrogen storage analysis; Characterization from Table 1 (main-4.png, p. 3), N2 at 77 K on Micromeritics ASAP 2020: S_BET 3503 m2/g (abstract prints 3508 m2/g; Table 1, Section 3.1 text, Section 3.3 and Table 2 print 3503); micropore volume = V_DR (DR) 1.10 cm3/g; total pore volume = V0.99 1.68 cm3/g; Vmeso 0.58 cm3/g (= V0.99 - V_DR); EA (characteristic energy) 20.24 kJ/mol; average micropore diameter L0 1.22 nm (printed L0 values match Stoeckli L0 = 10.8/(E0 - 11.4) applied to the printed EA); V_DR/V0.99 0.66; S_BET and pore volumes with a 'typical, maximum, uncertainty of 3 %'; BET applied to the adsorption branch, no P/P0 range printed; N2 outgassing 523 K for 48 h; H2 degassing: 'outgassed under a primary vacuum at 350 °C for 24 h' (no end pressure printed); uncertainty: 'Repeatability was always found to be very satisfactory, leading to errors lower than 3% on each measurement' (relative, so uncertainty_wt_pct left empty); basis not named in the paper; pressure not called gauge, taken as absolute; measuring_lab_id from the corresponding-author mark (*) on M Fan, although the printed corresponding e-mail is weigang-zhao@fafu.edu.cn
measuring_lab_id: Fan group, Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University
